You're designing an implementation plan for Nxeon (hosting platform, /opt/nxeon, Next.js/TS/Prisma/Postgres, Proxmox+OVH backend). Two related features, to be scoped together but landed safely. This is planning only — do not write code, just produce a detailed, ordered implementation plan with exact file paths, function names, and a verification strategy for each phase.

## Background already established (do not re-investigate, treat as fact)

**Current IP model**: every server (VPS or game) is a separate Proxmox VM (`worker/index.ts` `provision()`, ~line 413-722). IP assignment: `wantDedicated = server.wantsDedicatedIp || (await _settingBool("dedicated_ip_default", true))` (worker/index.ts ~line 460, and again at the unsuspend path ~line 899). `dedicated_ip_default` has NO entry in `lib/settings.ts` SETTINGS_DEFAULTS today (bug of omission) and defaults to the inline literal `true`. Game orders (`lib/game-order.ts` line 277) already set `wantsDedicatedIp: false`, but because of the OR against the global default, **every game order still gets a dedicated IP today** unless the pool (see below) is empty.

**Dedicated IP pool**: `lib/dedicated-ip.ts` — a real local `DedicatedIp` table synced from OVH-purchased failover IPs (`OVH_IP_UNIT_COST_CENTS=239`, i.e. $2.39/mo real cost to Nxeon per IP). `allocateDedicatedIp(serverId, vmid)` atomically claims a FREE+CUSTOMER row or returns null (no on-the-fly OVH ordering). `releaseDedicatedIp()` returns it to the pool on suspend/delete. Idempotent: if server already holds an ASSIGNED IP with bound vMAC, returns it unchanged.

**NAT/port-forward system already exists and is mature**: `lib/nat-rules.ts` (pure planning/reconciliation, never flushes rules — guards a past "H5" incident where an unconditional flush blackholed the fleet), `worker/network.ts` `syncPortForwards()` (real iptables `NXEON_FWD` chain), `prisma/schema.prisma` `PortForward` model (serverId, globally-unique publicPort, guestPort, protocol), `lib/ipam.ts` `allocateSshPort()`/`allocateIp()` (transaction + Postgres advisory-lock guarded, pool `Node.sshPortStart..sshPortEnd` default 20000-29999), `lib/actions-server.ts` `addPortForward`/`deletePortForward` (existing CUSTOMER-FACING feature, max 10/server, enqueues a `SYNC_FORWARDS` job).

**The critical existing gap**: on a NAT-tier server today, the game's own fixed port is NOT auto-forwarded — `worker/index.ts` ~line 636-638 explicitly notes "a game's own port is forwarded only if the customer adds one" manually via `addPortForward`. This means simply flipping games to NAT-by-default would ship undeployed/unreachable servers unless auto-forwarding is built.

**Game ports today**: `lib/games.ts` `GAME_PORT: Record<GameFamily, {port:number; protocol:"tcp"|"udp"}>` — ONE port per family, but the actual source of truth (`prisma/seed-wave1-games.ts`/`seed-wave2-games.ts` `OsTemplate.setupScript`, raw `docker run -p ... ` strings) shows several families need MULTIPLE ports (ARK: 4 ports; 7 Days to Die: a contiguous TCP+UDP block 26900-26903; V Rising/Palworld/Conan/Unturned: a game+query port pair or trio). `GAME_PORT`'s single-port shape does not model this today. `worker/index.ts`'s `wrapDockerGameService` (~line 148-188) parses each family's `docker run -d --name X ...` string via regex to turn it into a systemd unit — any port-remapping design must not break this parsing.

**mc-router (free Minecraft tier) is NOT reusable for this**: it works via Minecraft-protocol hostname-sniffing on ONE shared port across many Docker containers on ONE shared host (`lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`) — architecturally unrelated to paid orders, which are full separate VMs. Do not propose adapting mc-router to non-Minecraft games; the plan must use the DNAT/PortForward model instead.

**Renewal billing** (`lib/renewal-charge.ts`, pure function, single source of truth for order/renewal/display): confirmed bug — the `isGame` branch (`gameTotalCents`) is "flat all-in" and currently has NO dedicated-IP surcharge line at all (unlike the VPS branch, which has `(server.dedicatedIp ? prices.ipMonthlyCents * months : 0)`). If a game server is sold a dedicated IP add-on without fixing this, the customer would get free dedicated IP forever after the first term.

**Existing "add a paid feature to an already-deployed server" pattern to reuse** (this is the template for the post-deploy IP purchase): `lib/disk-expand.ts` (`diskExpandQuote()` pure quote + `applyDiskExpand()` atomic wallet-debit/Invoice/Job-create) + `lib/actions-disk.ts` `expandServerDisk()` (ownership check, email-verification gate, rate limit, wallet-split, Stripe-or-wallet) + `worker/index.ts` `DISK_EXPAND` job handler (line ~1343, only advances the billable DB field AFTER the real work succeeds, refunds on terminal failure via `reconcileFailedDiskExpand`) + Stripe metadata key pattern (`nxeonDiskExpand`, classified in `classifyCheckoutSession`). Dedicated IP allocation is real hypervisor/OVH work (not a column flip), so it must follow THIS pattern, not the simpler column-flip `lib/backup-upgrade.ts` pattern. The actual Proxmox net0/ipconfig0 reconfigure logic for attaching a dedicated IP to a live VM already exists nearly verbatim in the unsuspend path (`worker/index.ts` ~line 902-916) and should be extracted/reused rather than rewritten.

**VPS wizard's existing dedicated-IP UI to mirror for the game wizard**: `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx` — props `dedicatedIpAvailable?: boolean; dedicatedIpPriceCents?: number` (~line 165), checkbox state `dedicatedIp` (~line 283), card UI gated on availability (~line 924-941), hidden form field, live-total inclusion (~line 435), coupon-preview inclusion (~line 549). Supplied from `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx` (~line 60-107): `dedicatedIpAvailable = (await db.dedicatedIp.count({status:"FREE",purpose:"CUSTOMER"})) > 0`.

**Settings convention**: every add-on price is an admin-configurable `lib/settings.ts` SETTINGS_DEFAULTS key read through a small accessor (e.g. `dedicatedIpMonthlyCents()` in lib/dedicated-ip.ts), never hardcoded. Admin UI: `components/admin/settings/DedicatedIpPanel.tsx` already has a "Monthly price (cents)" field wired to `dedicated_ip_price_cents`.

## Decisions the owner already made (build to these, do not re-ask)

1. **Pricing scope**: game-server dedicated IP gets its OWN separate price, independent of VPS's existing (currently free) dedicated-IP add-on. Do NOT reuse/overload `dedicated_ip_price_cents` for games — add a new setting (e.g. `dedicated_ip_price_cents_game`, default `299` = $2.99/mo) with its own accessor and its own admin UI field, following the exact same convention as the existing one. VPS's current $0 price and behavior must be completely unaffected.
2. **Post-deploy purchase scope**: build the "buy a dedicated IP for an already-deployed server" flow for BOTH VPS and game servers (one shared mechanism, product-agnostic), not just games — since VPS currently has no post-deploy purchase path for this either, and the mechanism is identical.

## What to design

### Part A — Migrate paid game servers to shared-IP-by-default (safe, phased)
Must NOT change any existing VPS behavior, and must NOT silently strip an IP from an already-provisioned game server that currently holds one. Explicitly design:
- How the `worker/index.ts` OR-with-global-default logic changes so games stop inheriting the VPS-wide `dedicated_ip_default` (which should stay `true`, unaffected) — i.e. games should only get a dedicated IP when `wantsDedicatedIp` is explicitly true (from the new $2.99/mo upsell), never from a global fallback.
- What must be verified about the suspend/unsuspend re-evaluation path (`worker/index.ts` ~840-960) BEFORE this ships, to guarantee an existing dedicated-IP game server never gets silently downgraded to NAT on a routine suspend/unsuspend cycle. Call this out as a mandatory pre-flight verification step, not an assumption.
- How to auto-forward the game's fixed port(s) at provision time for NAT-tier game servers (closing the documented gap), including how `GAME_PORT`'s single-port shape needs to become multi-port-capable to correctly handle ARK/7DTD/V Rising/Palworld/Conan/Unturned, and how that flows into an automatic `PortForward` row creation (reusing `lib/ipam.ts`'s allocator idiom, NOT requiring the customer to click anything).
- A staged rollout mechanism (e.g. a dedicated settings kill-switch, off by default) so this can be verified against real staging orders across a representative mix of single-port TCP, single-port UDP, and multi-port game families before it's turned on for real customers.
- What customer-facing surfaces need updating to show `ip:port` instead of an assumed default port (server connect-info display).

### Part B — $2.99/mo dedicated-IPv4 upsell
- Deploy-wizard changes for `GameDeployWizard.tsx` mirroring the existing VPS pattern, and the exact `lib/game-order.ts` (`GameOrderIntent`, `gameOrderQuote`, `placeGameOrder`) changes needed to price and persist it.
- The `renewal-charge.ts` fix required so game servers with a dedicated IP are actually billed for it every cycle (currently silently free due to the isGame-branch gap) — and a regression-test angle (this codebase has an existing `test/pricing-display-vs-charge.test.ts` precedent for exactly this class of bug; the plan should call for an analogous test).
- The new post-deploy purchase flow (VPS + game, shared mechanism) modeled on `lib/disk-expand.ts` + `lib/actions-disk.ts` + the `DISK_EXPAND` worker-job pattern, reusing the unsuspend path's Proxmox net0/ipconfig0 reconfigure logic rather than duplicating it. Needs: quote function, apply function (wallet debit + Invoice + Job), a new JobType, a worker handler, availability/pool-empty handling (mirroring the existing wizard's `dedicatedIpAvailable` check), and where the customer-facing "Add dedicated IP" button lives on the server-detail dashboard page.
- The new `dedicated_ip_price_cents_game` setting + admin UI field, following the exact existing convention.

Produce a concrete, phased, file-by-file plan. For each phase, state what should be verified before moving to the next (this is explicitly a "be safe about it" migration per the owner). Do not write actual code — describe the changes precisely enough that another engineer could implement them, and flag any remaining open risk or ambiguity you find.

119	/**
120	 * If a GAME OsTemplate's setupScript installs the game via a detached
121	 * `docker run -d --name <container> ...` (true for every game image today —
122	 * see the OsTemplate rows for minecraft/terraria/ark/etc., all `docker run -d`),
123	 * rewrite the invocation to `docker create` and append a generated systemd unit
124	 * that starts/stops the container.
125	 *
126	 * WHY THIS EXISTS: the whole game control panel — GAME_POWER start/stop/restart,
127	 * GAME_BACKUP, log tailing (lib/game-control.ts + worker/game-control.ts) —
128	 * resolves the running game exclusively via `systemctl cat <serviceHint>` /
129	 * `journalctl -u <unit>`. A bare `docker run -d` creates no systemd unit at all,
130	 * so every one of those lookups comes back empty and every control action fails
131	 * silently, on every game family, on every order. Found 2026-08-26 diagnosing a
132	 * customer's Terraria server (cmt9ss7ln000xhlrx0gch9fcx) that could never be
133	 * started/stopped from the dashboard even though PROVISION had completed
134	 * successfully — the container was in fact running, just entirely invisible to
135	 * systemd.
136	 *
137	 * The generated unit is named after the family's FIRST serviceHint, not the
138	 * docker container's own `--name` — the two don't always match (minecraft's
139	 * image runs as container "mc" but its control-spec hints are "minecraft" /
140	 * "minecraft-server") — so `systemctl cat <hint>` resolves regardless of what an
141	 * individual image's setup script happened to call its container.
142	 *
143	 * Intentionally conservative: any setupScript that doesn't match the exact
144	 * `docker run -d --name X ...` shape (or any non-game family, e.g. the
145	 * LAMP/WordPress/Caddy panel images that already install a real native systemd
146	 * service) is returned completely unchanged.
147	 */
148	function wrapDockerGameService(setupScript: string, family: string | null): string {
149	  if (!isGameFamily(family)) return setupScript;
150	  const unitName = controlSpec(family)?.serviceHints[0];
151	  if (!unitName) return setupScript;
152	
153	  const re = /docker run\s+(?:-d|--detach)\b(.*?)\s+--name[= ]("?)([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\2(.*)$/.exec(setupScript.trim());
154	  if (!re) return setupScript;
155	  const [full, before, , containerName, after] = re;
156	  const matchIndex = setupScript.indexOf(full);
157	  if (matchIndex < 0) return setupScript;
158	
159	  // Strip docker's own restart policy — systemd now owns restart semantics for
160	  // this container, and leaving both in place makes the two supervisors fight
161	  // over a crash-looping process.
162	  const cleanedAfter = after.replace(/\s*--restart(?:=|\s+)\S+/, "");
163	  const createCmd = `docker create --name ${containerName}${before}${cleanedAfter}`.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
164	
165	  const prefix = setupScript.slice(0, matchIndex);
166	  const unit = [
167	    `cat > /etc/systemd/system/${unitName}.service <<'NXUNIT'`,
168	    "[Unit]",
169	    `Description=Nxeon game service (docker: ${containerName})`,
170	    "After=docker.service",
171	    "Requires=docker.service",
172	    "",
173	    "[Service]",
174	    `ExecStart=/usr/bin/docker start -a ${containerName}`,
175	    `ExecStop=/usr/bin/docker stop -t 30 ${containerName}`,
176	    "Restart=always",
177	    "RestartSec=5",
178	    "TimeoutStartSec=0",
179	    "",
180	    "[Install]",
181	    "WantedBy=multi-user.target",
182	    "NXUNIT",
183	    "systemctl daemon-reload",
184	    `systemctl enable --now ${unitName}`,
185	  ].join("\n");
186	
187	  return `${prefix}${createCmd}\n${unit}`;
188	}

220	    `curl -fsSL "${appUrl}/dl/nxeon-shipper.service" -o /etc/systemd/system/nxeon-shipper.service`,

274	  // eats a small root disk) turns a hard kill into slow-but-alive. Idempotent:

280	    "[ -e /swapfile ] && exit 0",
281	    'MEM_MB=$(awk "/MemTotal/{print int(\\$2/1024)}" /proc/meminfo 2>/dev/null || echo 1024)',

I'm realizing the release-on-suspend logic runs unconditionally whenever OVH is configured and the server had an IP, regardless of `wantDedicated`, which means the `alreadyHas` check on unsuspend will always be false since the IP was already released — so `wantDedicated` alone decides whether it's reclaimed, which could cause unexpected behavior if the global default changes while a server's own preference is false.

If a game server only had a dedicated IP because of the OR-with-global-default logic, then after a suspend/unsuspend cycle it would silently fall back to NAT once that OR is removed, since `wantDedicated` would now be false. This is exactly the risk flagged earlier, so the fix needs a backfill step that sets `wantsDedicatedIp = true` on existing game servers that currently hold a dedicated IP before changing the OR logic. I want to confirm the schema has this `wantsDedicatedIp` field alongside `gamePlanId` and the dedicated IP relation.

## Open risks / ambiguities to flag before implementation starts

1. **No "remove dedicated IP" path exists.** Once a VPS or game server buys the Part B4 upsell, there is no self-service downgrade back to NAT. `applyDedicatedIpPurchase`/the UI copy should say so explicitly (as disk expansion does for its own one-way growth) until/unless a companion "Remove dedicated IP" flow is scoped — that's a third feature, out of scope here, but the UI must not imply reversibility it doesn't have.
2. **Network downtime during the live attach.** Unlike disk expansion (no VM restart needed), attaching a dedicated IP to an already-running server requires a stop/reconfigure/start cycle (per the unsuspend precedent). This is real, visible downtime (probably 30–90s) that the disk-expand pattern doesn't have to warn about — the purchase UI must say so before charging, not just in a post-purchase notification.
3. **`MAX_FORWARDS_PER_SERVER` interaction with AUTO rows.** Even after excluding `origin: AUTO` from the customer's count, a family needing 6 rows (unturned) plus a customer wanting several of their own now shares one flat cap of 10 customer-added rows — unchanged from today's VPS behavior, but worth a product decision on whether the customer-facing cap should be raised, left alone, or made per-origin-visible in the UI so it isn't confusing ("why can I only add 4 more when the limit is 10?").
4. **`gameOrderQuote`'s composed `chargeCents`.** Whether the dedicated-IP add-on folds into the single `chargeCents` scalar (simplest, matches `lib/order.ts`'s existing `ipCents` treatment) or needs its own discrete field threaded through Stripe metadata and `GameOrderPrice` is a real design choice with downstream effects on the receipt/invoice line-item breakdown for a card-paid game order with the add-on — recommend folding it in (matching VPS) unless product wants a discrete invoice line at ORDER time too (Part B3 already gives it one at RENEWAL time).
5. **Placement of the game wizard's checkbox.** Recommended above to make it more visible than the VPS wizard's "Advanced options" disclosure (since it's a real charge, not a currently-free toggle) — this is a product/UX call, not purely technical, and should be confirmed before implementation.
6. **A0.3's retry-race guard and B4's live-reconfigure both read/write `DedicatedIp`/`Server.ipAddress` outside of `lib/ipam.ts`'s advisory-lock scope.** `allocateDedicatedIp`'s own transaction covers the *pool claim*, but the Proxmox config POST + Server row update afterward is not itself transactional against a concurrent suspend/delete of the same server firing at the same moment (existing behavior for `provision()`/`suspend()` already has this property — B4 doesn't make it worse, but it's worth a `pending` job-count guard in `addDedicatedIp`'s action layer, which is already planned above, as the practical mitigation rather than a new lock).
